definition: Sketch Engine is a corpus manager and text analysis software developed by Lexical Computing since 2003.
details: Its purpose is to enable people studying language behaviour (lexicographers, researchers in corpus linguistics, translators or language learners) to search large text collections according to complex and linguistically motivated queries. Sketch Engine gained its name after one of the key features, word sketches: one-page, automatic, corpus-derived summaries of a word's grammatical and collocational behaviour. Currently, it supports and provides corpora in over 100 languages.

explainer.lead: Sketch Engine is a corpus manager and text analysis software developed by Lexical Computing since 2003. It matters because it lets lexicographers, corpus linguists, translators and language learners search large text collections with complex, linguistically motivated queries.

tiers.eli5: It's a search engine for huge piles of real text, built so you can ask grammar-style questions rather than just look for keywords. It's named after its word sketches: one-page summaries of how a word behaves.
tiers.practitioner: Users query large corpora to study a word's grammatical and collocational behaviour, with word sketches giving automatic one-page summaries. A pitfall is that findings reflect the corpus you choose, so conclusions depend on which text collection the queries run against.
tiers.paperLevel: A corpus manager and text analysis platform; its defining feature, word sketches, produces one-page automatic corpus-derived summaries of a word's grammatical and collocational behaviour, and it supports corpora in over 100 languages.

explainer.example: A translator looks up an unfamiliar word in Sketch Engine and reads its word sketch to see which grammatical patterns and collocations it typically appears in.
